```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, dpi = 110,
  fig.path = "outputs/figures/"

```

This notebook implements the six-stage pipeline proposed in the project
report: **clean → tokenize & tf-idf → document-term matrix → LSA topics →
lexicon sentiment → validation**. Every number and chart below is produced by
running the code on the data.

# Setup

```{r packages}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(tidytext)
library(Matrix)
library(irlba)        # fast truncated SVD on a sparse matrix
library(wordcloud)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(reshape2)
library(caret)        # confusion matrices
library(glmnet)       # regularised logistic regression
library(lime)         # local explanations of the classifier

set.seed(2026)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

N_PER_CLASS <- 5000   # reviews sampled per class (report: 5k-10k total is enough)
K_TOPICS    <- 10     # number of LSA topics kept (justified by the scree plot)
```

Sentiment lexicons. Bing ships with **tidytext**; AFINN and NRC are fetched
once with **textdata** by `get_lexicons.R` and cached in `lexicons/`.

```{r lexicons}
afinn <- readRDS("lexicons/afinn/afinn.rds")
bing  <- get_sentiments("bing")
nrc   <- readRDS("lexicons/nrc/nrc.rds")

tibble(lexicon = c("AFINN", "Bing", "NRC"),
       words   = c(nrow(afinn), nrow(bing), n_distinct(nrc$word)),
       scoring = c("integer -5 .. +5", "positive / negative",
                   "positive / negative + 8 emotions"))
```

# Stage 1 – Explore and clean the text

```{r load}
reviews_all <- read_csv("data/imdb_reviews.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

reviews <- reviews_all |>
  group_by(sentiment) |>
  slice_sample(n = N_PER_CLASS) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

cat("Full dataset:", nrow(reviews_all), "reviews | analysed sample:",
    nrow(reviews), "reviews\n")
count(reviews_all, sentiment, name = "reviews_in_full_dataset")
```

```{r clean}
clean_text <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") |>      # HTML tags such as <br />
    str_to_lower() |>
    str_replace_all("[^a-z' ]", " ") |>      # punctuation and numbers
    str_replace_all("(^| )'+|'+( |$)", " ") |>
    str_squish()
}

reviews <- reviews |>
  mutate(clean   = clean_text(review),
         n_words = str_count(clean, "\\S+"))

reviews |> select(review) |> slice(1) |> pull() |> str_trunc(400) |> cat()
cat("\n\n--- after cleaning ---\n\n")
reviews |> select(clean)  |> slice(1) |> pull() |> str_trunc(400) |> cat()
```

```{r eda-summary}
reviews |>
  group_by(sentiment) |>
  summarise(reviews       = n(),
            mean_words    = round(mean(n_words)),
            median_words  = median(n_words),
            min_words     = min(n_words),
            max_words     = max(n_words),
            mean_stars    = round(mean(rating), 2))
```

```{r eda-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(reviews, aes(n_words, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, alpha = 0.75, position = "identity") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1200)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(negative = "#d1495b", positive = "#00798c")) +
  labs(title = "Review length by sentiment",
       subtitle = "Both classes have a similar long-tailed length distribution",
       x = "Words per review (after cleaning)", y = "Reviews", fill = NULL)

reviews |>
  count(rating, sentiment) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(rating), n, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(negative = "#d1495b", positive = "#00798c")) +
  labs(title = "Star ratings in the sample",
       subtitle = "Labels come from ratings: <= 4 stars negative, >= 7 positive (neutral 5-6 excluded)",
       x = "Stars", y = "Reviews", fill = NULL)
```

# Stage 2 – Tokenize, word frequency and tf-idf

`unnest_tokens()` gives one word per row. Two token tables are kept:
`tokens_all` (every word, used for sentiment so that words such as *not* stay
available) and `tokens` (stop words removed, used for frequency, tf-idf and LSA).

```{r tokenize}
tokens_all <- reviews |>
  select(id, sentiment, clean) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, clean) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(position = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

# Domain words that appear everywhere and carry no topic information
domain_stop <- tibble(word = c("movie", "movies", "film", "films", "br",
                               "time", "watch", "watching", "watched",
                               "people", "lot", "makes", "bit", "thing"))

tokens <- tokens_all |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(str_length(word) > 2)

cat("Tokens (all words):", format(nrow(tokens_all), big.mark = ","),
    "\nTokens (stop words removed):", format(nrow(tokens), big.mark = ","),
    "\nDistinct words:", format(n_distinct(tokens$word), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

```{r word-freq, fig.height = 5.5}
word_counts <- tokens |> count(word, sort = TRUE)

word_counts |>
  slice_head(n = 25) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, fct_reorder(word, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#30638e") +
  labs(title = "Most frequent words (stop words removed)",
       x = "Occurrences", y = NULL)
```

**Zipf's law.** A handful of words dominate raw counts – frequency falls
roughly in proportion to 1 / rank – which is why raw counts alone are a poor
measure of how informative a word is.

```{r zipf, fig.height = 4.5}
zipf <- tokens_all |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), freq = n / sum(n))

zipf_fit <- lm(log10(freq) ~ log10(rank), data = filter(zipf, rank <= 5000))

ggplot(zipf, aes(rank, freq)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#30638e", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(intercept = coef(zipf_fit)[1], slope = coef(zipf_fit)[2],
              linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Zipf's law in IMDb reviews",
       subtitle = sprintf("Fitted log-log slope = %.2f (Zipf's law predicts about -1)",
                          coef(zipf_fit)[2]),
       x = "Word rank (log scale)", y = "Term frequency (log scale)")
```

**tf-idf.** `bind_tf_idf()` weights each word in each review by how often it
appears there (*tf*) and how rare it is across all reviews (*idf*). Words
that are distinctive for a few reviews score high; words found everywhere
score close to zero.

```{r tfidf}
review_tfidf <- tokens |>
  count(id, word) |>
  bind_tf_idf(word, id, n)

# Words that are both reasonably common and distinctive where they occur
review_tfidf |>
  group_by(word) |>
  summarise(reviews = n(), idf = first(idf), mean_tf_idf = mean(tf_idf)) |>
  filter(reviews >= 50) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_tf_idf)) |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  mutate(across(c(idf, mean_tf_idf), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Distinctive vocabulary of each star rating (each rating group treated as one
"document"):

```{r tfidf-rating, fig.height = 7}
tokens |>
  left_join(select(reviews, id, rating), by = "id") |>
  count(rating, word) |>
  filter(n >= 15) |>
  bind_tf_idf(word, rating, n) |>
  group_by(rating) |>
  slice_max(tf_idf, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(rating = paste(rating, "stars"),
         word   = reorder_within(word, tf_idf, rating)) |>
  ggplot(aes(tf_idf, word, fill = rating)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  facet_wrap(~ rating, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Highest tf-idf words for each star rating",
       x = "tf-idf", y = NULL)
```

# Stage 3 – Document-term matrix

Rows are reviews, columns are terms, values are tf-idf weights. Very rare
terms (in fewer than 20 reviews) and near-universal ones (more than 30 % of
reviews) are dropped, and each row is scaled to unit length so that long
reviews do not dominate the decomposition.

```{r dtm}
doc_freq <- tokens |>
  anti_join(domain_stop, by = "word") |>
  distinct(id, word) |>
  count(word, name = "df")

vocab <- doc_freq |>
  filter(df >= 20, df <= 0.30 * nrow(reviews)) |>
  pull(word) |>
  sort()

idf_lookup <- review_tfidf |>
  filter(word %in% vocab) |>
  distinct(word, idf)
idf_vec <- setNames(idf_lookup$idf, idf_lookup$word)[vocab]

# Turns any character vector of reviews into an L2-normalised tf-idf matrix
# over the fixed vocabulary (re-used later by the classifier and LIME).
text_to_dtm <- function(texts) {
  td <- tibble(doc = seq_along(texts), text = clean_text(texts)) |>
    unnest_tokens(word, text) |>
    filter(word %in% vocab) |>
    count(doc, word) |>
    group_by(doc) |>
    mutate(w = n / sum(n) * idf_vec[word]) |>
    ungroup()
  m <- sparseMatrix(i = td$doc, j = match(td$word, vocab), x = td$w,
                    dims = c(length(texts), length(vocab)),
                    dimnames = list(NULL, vocab))
  norms <- sqrt(rowSums(m^2))
  norms[norms == 0] <- 1
  Diagonal(x = 1 / norms) %*% m
}

dtm <- text_to_dtm(reviews$review)

cat(sprintf("Document-term matrix: %s reviews x %s terms, %.2f%% non-zero\n",
            comma(nrow(dtm)), comma(ncol(dtm)),
            100 * length(dtm@x) / prod(dim(dtm))))
```

# Stage 4 – Topic discovery with LSA

LSA factorises the matrix with a truncated SVD: **A ≈ U~k~ Σ~k~ V~k~^T^**.
`irlba` computes the leading 50 singular vectors directly on the sparse
matrix, which is far cheaper than a full dense SVD.

```{r svd}
svd50 <- irlba(dtm, nv = 50, nu = 50)

total_var <- sum(dtm^2)                      # squared Frobenius norm
scree <- tibble(dimension = 1:50,
                var_explained = svd50$d^2 / total_var) |>
  mutate(cumulative = cumsum(var_explained))
```

```{r scree, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(scree, aes(dimension, var_explained)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#30638e") +
  geom_point(colour = "#30638e") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = K_TOPICS, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d1495b") +
  annotate("text", x = K_TOPICS + 0.5, y = max(scree$var_explained),
           label = paste("k =", K_TOPICS), hjust = 0, colour = "#d1495b") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Scree plot of the LSA dimensions",
       subtitle = "Variance explained flattens after roughly the first ten dimensions",
       x = "LSA dimension", y = "Share of total variance")

scree |> filter(dimension %in% c(1, 5, 10, 20, 50)) |>
  mutate(across(-dimension, \(x) percent(x, accuracy = 0.01)))
```

Text matrices have a very flat spectrum, so k cannot be chosen from a
variance target such as 80 %: the scree plot's elbow is used instead, and
**k = `r K_TOPICS`** is kept.

**Raw LSA dimensions.** Loadings can be positive *or* negative, and the first
dimension simply captures the vocabulary shared by all reviews. This is the
interpretability problem the report mentions:

```{r raw-dims}
raw_v <- svd50$v[, 1:4]
rownames(raw_v) <- vocab
lapply(1:4, function(j) {
  tibble(dimension = j,
         `top positive terms` = paste(names(sort(raw_v[, j], decreasing = TRUE))[1:8], collapse = ", "),
         `top negative terms` = paste(names(sort(raw_v[, j]))[1:8], collapse = ", "))
}) |> bind_rows()
```

**Rotated topics.** To make the k dimensions readable, the term loadings are
rotated with **varimax** (a standard step in LSA and factor analysis). The
rotation spans exactly the same k-dimensional space, but concentrates each
topic on a smaller set of words. Each topic is oriented so its strongest
words load positively.

```{r rotate}
V <- svd50$v[, 1:K_TOPICS]
rot <- varimax(V, normalize = FALSE)
loadings <- unclass(rot$loadings)
rownames(loadings) <- vocab

orientation <- apply(loadings, 2, function(col) sign(col[which.max(abs(col))]))
loadings <- sweep(loadings, 2, orientation, `*`)
colnames(loadings) <- paste0("T", 1:K_TOPICS)

topic_terms <- as_tibble(loadings, rownames = "term") |>
  pivot_longer(-term, names_to = "topic", values_to = "loading") |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(loading, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

topic_terms |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  summarise(top_terms = paste(term, collapse = ", ")) |>
  arrange(as.integer(str_remove(topic, "T")))
```

Each topic is named from its highest-loading terms:

```{r labels}
topic_labels <- c(
  T1  = "Acting & performances",
  T2  = "Bad acting & wasted money",
  T3  = "TV series & episodes",
  T4  = "Horror & slashers",
  T5  = "Comedy & humour",
  T6  = "Book adaptations",
  T7  = "Family & thriller plots",
  T8  = "Music, love & family viewing",
  T9  = "Action & special effects",
  T10 = "War, history & documentaries"
)
topic_labels
```

```{r topic-terms-plot, fig.height = 11}
topic_terms |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(loading, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = factor(topic_labels[topic], levels = topic_labels),
         term  = reorder_within(term, loading, label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(loading, term, fill = label)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Top terms for each LSA topic (varimax-rotated loadings)",
       x = "Term loading", y = NULL)
```

Every review gets a score on each topic (its projection onto the rotated
loadings) and is assigned to the topic it scores highest on.

```{r assign}
doc_scores <- as.matrix(dtm %*% loadings)

reviews <- reviews |>
  mutate(topic       = colnames(doc_scores)[max.col(doc_scores, ties.method = "first")],
         topic_label = factor(topic_labels[topic], levels = topic_labels),
         topic_score = apply(doc_scores, 1, max))

reviews |>
  count(topic_label) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, fct_rev(topic_label))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#30638e") +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Reviews assigned to each topic (dominant topic)",
       x = "Reviews", y = NULL)
```

Example review snippets for each topic (the review scoring highest on it):

```{r examples}
reviews |>
  group_by(topic_label) |>
  slice_max(topic_score, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(topic = topic_label, sentiment,
            snippet = str_trunc(str_squish(str_replace_all(review, "<[^>]+>", " ")), 180))
```

# Stage 5 – Sentiment analysis with three dictionaries

Each review is scored with every lexicon using **all** of its words
(stop-word lists contain words like *not* and *well* that matter for opinion).

* **AFINN** – sum of word scores (-5 … +5)
* **Bing** – positive words minus negative words
* **NRC** – positive minus negative words, plus counts for 8 emotions

```{r score}
words_only <- select(tokens_all, id, word)

afinn_scores <- words_only |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(afinn = sum(value), afinn_words = n())

bing_scores <- words_only |>
  inner_join(bing, by = "word") |>
  count(id, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  transmute(id, bing = positive - negative, bing_words = positive + negative)

nrc_polarity <- words_only |>
  inner_join(filter(nrc, sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")),
             by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(id, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  transmute(id, nrc = positive - negative)

nrc_emotions <- words_only |>
  inner_join(filter(nrc, !sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")),
             by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(id, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

scored <- reviews |>
  select(id, sentiment, rating, n_words, topic, topic_label) |>
  left_join(afinn_scores, by = "id") |>
  left_join(bing_scores,  by = "id") |>
  left_join(nrc_polarity, by = "id") |>
  mutate(across(c(afinn, afinn_words, bing, bing_words, nrc), \(x) coalesce(x, 0)))

scored |>
  group_by(sentiment) |>
  summarise(across(c(afinn, bing, nrc), \(x) round(mean(x), 2), .names = "mean_{.col}"))
```

```{r top-sentiment-words, fig.height = 5}
words_only |>
  inner_join(bing, by = "word") |>
  count(word, sentiment, sort = TRUE) |>
  group_by(sentiment) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(word = reorder_within(word, n, sentiment)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, word, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(negative = "#d1495b", positive = "#00798c")) +
  facet_wrap(~ sentiment, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Most common positive and negative words (Bing lexicon)",
       x = "Occurrences", y = NULL)
```

Note *plot*, *funny* and *like*: lexicon words whose meaning in a movie
review is not always opinion (see Limitations).

```{r wordcloud-all, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7}
par(mar = rep(0, 4))
word_counts |>
  anti_join(domain_stop, by = "word") |>
  with(wordcloud(word, n, max.words = 120, random.order = FALSE,
                 rot.per = 0.15, colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2")))
```

```{r wordcloud-compare, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7}
par(mar = rep(0, 4))
words_only |>
  inner_join(bing, by = "word") |>
  count(word, sentiment, sort = TRUE) |>
  acast(word ~ sentiment, value.var = "n", fill = 0) |>
  comparison.cloud(colors = c("#d1495b", "#00798c"), max.words = 150,
                   title.size = 1.6)
```

**NRC emotions.** Share of emotion words falling into each emotion, by the
true review label:

```{r nrc-emotions, fig.height = 4.5}
tokens_all |>
  rename(review_label = sentiment) |>
  inner_join(filter(nrc, !sentiment %in% c("positive", "negative")),
             by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(review_label, emotion = sentiment) |>
  group_by(review_label) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(share, fct_reorder(emotion, share), fill = review_label)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(negative = "#d1495b", positive = "#00798c")) +
  labs(title = "NRC emotion profile of positive vs negative reviews",
       x = "Share of emotion words", y = NULL, fill = "True label")
```

## Sentiment by topic

The three lexicon scores have different scales, so each is standardised
(z-score) before being averaged per topic. The share of truly positive reviews
in each topic is shown alongside as ground truth.

```{r topic-sentiment}
topic_sentiment <- scored |>
  mutate(across(c(afinn, bing, nrc), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x)), .names = "{.col}_z")) |>
  group_by(topic_label) |>
  summarise(reviews        = n(),
            pct_positive   = mean(sentiment == "positive"),
            mean_stars     = mean(rating),
            AFINN          = mean(afinn_z),
            Bing           = mean(bing_z),
            NRC            = mean(nrc_z)) |>
  arrange(desc(AFINN))

topic_sentiment |>
  mutate(pct_positive = percent(pct_positive, accuracy = 0.1),
         across(c(mean_stars, AFINN, Bing, NRC), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r topic-sentiment-plot, fig.height = 5.5}
topic_sentiment |>
  pivot_longer(c(AFINN, Bing, NRC), names_to = "lexicon", values_to = "z") |>
  mutate(topic_label = fct_reorder(topic_label, z, .fun = mean)) |>
  ggplot(aes(z, topic_label, colour = lexicon)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(AFINN = "#30638e", Bing = "#edae49", NRC = "#d1495b")) +
  labs(title = "Topic versus sentiment",
       subtitle = "Mean standardised sentiment score of the reviews in each topic (right = more positive)",
       x = "Mean sentiment (z-score)", y = NULL, colour = "Lexicon")
```

```{r topic-truth-plot, fig.height = 5}
topic_sentiment |>
  mutate(topic_label = fct_reorder(topic_label, pct_positive)) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct_positive, topic_label, fill = pct_positive)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct_positive, accuracy = 1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#d1495b", mid = "grey85", high = "#00798c", midpoint = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Which themes are praised and which are criticised?",
       subtitle = "Share of reviews in each topic that are truly positive (dataset labels)",
       x = "Positive reviews", y = NULL)
```

```{r topic-emotion-heatmap, fig.height = 5}
scored |>
  select(id, topic_label) |>
  left_join(nrc_emotions, by = "id") |>
  mutate(across(-c(id, topic_label), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L))) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, topic_label), names_to = "emotion", values_to = "n") |>
  group_by(topic_label, emotion) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(emotion, topic_label, fill = share)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(share, accuracy = 1)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#30638e", labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "NRC emotion mix within each topic",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Share")
```

# Stage 6 – Validation against the dataset labels

A review is predicted **positive** when its lexicon score is above 0 and
**negative** otherwise.

```{r validate}
truth <- factor(scored$sentiment, levels = c("negative", "positive"))
predict_label <- function(score) factor(ifelse(score > 0, "positive", "negative"),
                                        levels = c("negative", "positive"))

cms <- list(
  AFINN = confusionMatrix(predict_label(scored$afinn), truth, positive = "positive"),
  Bing  = confusionMatrix(predict_label(scored$bing),  truth, positive = "positive"),
  NRC   = confusionMatrix(predict_label(scored$nrc),   truth, positive = "positive")
)

lexicon_accuracy <- tibble(
  method      = names(cms),
  accuracy    = sapply(cms, \(cm) cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
  sensitivity = sapply(cms, \(cm) cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
  specificity = sapply(cms, \(cm) cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
  kappa       = sapply(cms, \(cm) cm$overall["Kappa"]),
  zero_score  = c(mean(scored$afinn == 0), mean(scored$bing == 0), mean(scored$nrc == 0))
)

lexicon_accuracy |> mutate(across(-method, \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

Sensitivity is recall on positive reviews; specificity is recall on negative
reviews. AFINN and NRC lean strongly positive (high sensitivity, low
specificity): negative reviews still use many positive words ("good actors,
*but*…"). Bing is the most balanced of the three, partly because it counts
words such as *plot* and *funny* as negative.

```{r confusion-plot, fig.height = 4}
lapply(names(cms), function(m) {
  as_tibble(cms[[m]]$table) |> mutate(method = m)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  group_by(method, Reference) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(Reference, Prediction, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(comma(n), "\n(", percent(pct, accuracy = 1), ")")), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#30638e", guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ method) +
  labs(title = "Confusion matrices of the lexicon methods",
       subtitle = "Percentages are of each true class",
       x = "True label", y = "Predicted label")
```

## Improvement 1: simple negation handling

Dictionary methods miss negation (*not good*). A small fix: flip the AFINN
score of a word when one of the two preceding words is a negator.

```{r negation}
negators <- c("not", "no", "never", "without", "nothing", "isn't", "wasn't",
              "aren't", "don't", "doesn't", "didn't", "can't", "couldn't",
              "won't", "wouldn't", "hardly", "nor", "neither")

afinn_neg <- words_only |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(prev1 = lag(word, 1), prev2 = lag(word, 2)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  mutate(negated = coalesce(prev1 %in% negators | prev2 %in% negators, FALSE),
         value   = if_else(negated, -value, value)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(afinn_negation = sum(value), negated_words = sum(negated))

scored <- scored |>
  left_join(afinn_neg, by = "id") |>
  mutate(afinn_negation = coalesce(afinn_negation, 0))

cm_neg <- confusionMatrix(predict_label(scored$afinn_negation), truth, positive = "positive")

words_only |>
  group_by(id) |> mutate(prev1 = lag(word)) |> ungroup() |>
  filter(prev1 %in% negators) |>
  inner_join(afinn, by = "word") |>
  count(phrase = paste(prev1, word), value, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

tibble(method = c("AFINN", "AFINN + negation"),
       accuracy = c(cms$AFINN$overall["Accuracy"], cm_neg$overall["Accuracy"])) |>
  mutate(accuracy = round(accuracy, 3))
```

## Improvement 2: a supervised classifier (logistic regression)

The lexicons use no training data. For comparison, a lasso-regularised
logistic regression is trained on the same tf-idf document-term matrix
(80 % train / 20 % test, split stratified by label).

```{r logreg}
y <- factor(reviews$sentiment, levels = c("negative", "positive"))
train_idx <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)[, 1]

cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(dtm[train_idx, ], y[train_idx], family = "binomial",
                    alpha = 1, type.measure = "class", nfolds = 5)

test_prob <- predict(cv_fit, dtm[-train_idx, ], s = "lambda.min", type = "response")[, 1]
test_pred <- factor(ifelse(test_prob > 0.5, "positive", "negative"),
                    levels = c("negative", "positive"))
cm_glm <- confusionMatrix(test_pred, y[-train_idx], positive = "positive")
cm_glm
```

```{r logreg-coefs, fig.height = 6}
coefs <- coef(cv_fit, s = "lambda.min")
coef_tbl <- tibble(term = rownames(coefs), weight = as.numeric(coefs)) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)", weight != 0)

cat("Terms kept by the lasso:", nrow(coef_tbl), "of", length(vocab), "\n")

bind_rows(slice_max(coef_tbl, weight, n = 15), slice_min(coef_tbl, weight, n = 15)) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(weight > 0, "pushes towards positive", "pushes towards negative")) |>
  ggplot(aes(weight, fct_reorder(term, weight), fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("pushes towards negative" = "#d1495b",
                               "pushes towards positive" = "#00798c")) +
  labs(title = "Strongest words in the logistic regression",
       x = "Coefficient", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

```{r all-accuracy, fig.height = 4}
accuracy_summary <- tibble(
  method   = c("AFINN", "Bing", "NRC", "AFINN + negation", "Logistic regression (test set)"),
  type     = c(rep("Lexicon (no training)", 4), "Supervised"),
  accuracy = c(cms$AFINN$overall["Accuracy"], cms$Bing$overall["Accuracy"],
               cms$NRC$overall["Accuracy"],   cm_neg$overall["Accuracy"],
               cm_glm$overall["Accuracy"]),
  lower_95 = c(cms$AFINN$overall["AccuracyLower"], cms$Bing$overall["AccuracyLower"],
               cms$NRC$overall["AccuracyLower"],   cm_neg$overall["AccuracyLower"],
               cm_glm$overall["AccuracyLower"]),
  upper_95 = c(cms$AFINN$overall["AccuracyUpper"], cms$Bing$overall["AccuracyUpper"],
               cms$NRC$overall["AccuracyUpper"],   cm_neg$overall["AccuracyUpper"],
               cm_glm$overall["AccuracyUpper"])
)

ggplot(accuracy_summary, aes(accuracy, fct_reorder(method, accuracy), colour = type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_95, xmax = upper_95), height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(accuracy, accuracy = 0.1)), vjust = -1, size = 3.5,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0.45, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Lexicon (no training)" = "#edae49", Supervised = "#30638e")) +
  labs(title = "Sentiment accuracy against the IMDb labels",
       subtitle = "With 95% confidence intervals; dashed line = chance (balanced classes)",
       x = "Accuracy", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

## Explaining predictions with LIME

LIME perturbs a review by removing words and fits a simple local model to see
which words drove the classifier's decision for that particular review.

```{r lime, fig.height = 10}
lime_model <- structure(list(fit = cv_fit), class = "imdb_lasso")

registerS3method("model_type", "imdb_lasso",
                 function(x, ...) "classification", envir = asNamespace("lime"))
registerS3method("predict_model", "imdb_lasso", function(x, newdata, type, ...) {
  p <- predict(x$fit, text_to_dtm(newdata), s = "lambda.min", type = "response")[, 1]
  data.frame(negative = 1 - p, positive = p)
}, envir = asNamespace("lime"))

test_reviews <- reviews[-train_idx, ] |>
  mutate(prob = test_prob, review_text = str_replace_all(review, "<[^>]+>", " "))

# one confident positive, one confident negative, one the model got wrong
to_explain <- bind_rows(
  test_reviews |> filter(sentiment == "positive", n_words < 150) |> slice_max(prob, n = 1),
  test_reviews |> filter(sentiment == "negative", n_words < 150) |> slice_min(prob, n = 1),
  test_reviews |> filter(n_words < 150,
                         (sentiment == "positive") != (prob > 0.5)) |> slice(1)
)

explainer <- lime(reviews$review[train_idx], lime_model)
explanation <- explain(to_explain$review_text, explainer, n_labels = 1,
                       n_features = 8, n_permutations = 1000)

plot_features(explanation, ncol = 1)

to_explain |>
  transmute(case = c("confident positive", "confident negative", "misclassified"),
            true_label = sentiment, predicted_p_positive = round(prob, 3),
            text = str_trunc(str_squish(review_text), 300))
```

# Summary of findings

```{r summary, echo = FALSE}
best_topic  <- topic_sentiment |> slice_max(pct_positive, n = 1)
worst_topic <- topic_sentiment |> slice_min(pct_positive, n = 1)
```

* **Topics.** LSA with k = `r K_TOPICS` varimax-rotated dimensions recovers
  interpretable themes (see the topic chart). The most praised theme is
  **`r best_topic$topic_label`** (`r percent(best_topic$pct_positive, 1)` of its
  reviews are positive); the most criticised is **`r worst_topic$topic_label`**
  (`r percent(worst_topic$pct_positive, 1)` positive).
* **Lexicon sentiment.** Accuracy against the labels: AFINN
  `r percent(cms$AFINN$overall[["Accuracy"]], 0.1)`, Bing
  `r percent(cms$Bing$overall[["Accuracy"]], 0.1)`, NRC
  `r percent(cms$NRC$overall[["Accuracy"]], 0.1)`. AFINN and NRC over-predict
  the positive class; Bing is the most balanced and the most accurate lexicon. Simple negation handling moves AFINN to
  `r percent(cm_neg$overall[["Accuracy"]], 0.1)`.
* **Supervised model.** Lasso logistic regression on the same tf-idf features
  reaches `r percent(cm_glm$overall[["Accuracy"]], 0.1)` on held-out reviews,
  showing how much a model trained on movie-review language gains over
  general-purpose dictionaries.
* **Limitations confirmed.** Words like *plot*, *funny*, *like* and *kill* are
  mis-scored by lexicons in a movie context; LSA needs a rotation and manual
  judgement of k to give readable topics; LDA, transformer sentiment models and
  aspect-level sentiment remain the natural next steps.

